text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe government, its finances in crisis because of runaway spending, has sold more than 30 Mercedes Benz cars to cabinet ministers and other government officials for as little as Z$6,000 each instead of the market price of around Z$250,000, losing more than Z$7 million in the process, sources told the Financial Gazette.
- The government, through the Ministry of Information, Posts and Telecommunications, is actively considering dismissing suspended Zimbabwe Newspapers managing director Simba Makoni, insiders say.

- President Robert Mugabe has rescued former Zimbabwe Development Bank chief executive Xavier Kadhani, whose mansion in Harare was about to be sold, by facilitating the payment of Z$3 million Kadhani owed to the Central African Building Society in a long overdue mortgage bond, sources told the Financial Gazette on Wednesday.
- Zimbabwe paper manufacturing and converting giant Art Corporation has for the second year running posted a huge loss of Z$227 million during the financial year ended September 1996.
- Zimbabwe will receive a Z$1.2 billion loan from the European Investment Bank to assist viable private sector business ventures and development infrastructure.

- The decision by the World Bank to award Indian companies the bulk of a tender to supply Zimbabwean government institutions with drugs valued at Z$51 million has angered local pharmaceutical manufacturers.

- Zimbabwean president Robert Mugabe on Wednesday appealed to doctors and nurses to respect human life and not use patients as "sacrificial lambs" in bargaining for higher wages, but also acknowledged that doctors in the country were not well paid.
- The Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries says stiff retaliatory measures should be imposed to force South Africa into signing a new trade agreement with its neighbour.
